content: The text provided is a list of references formatted in a fragmented and non-standard way. 1. An update on human cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) virus infection was published in the Weekly Epidemiological Record on March 30, 2012, covering data from 2011 (Volume 87, Issue 12, Pages 117-128). 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released an overview of the emergence and characteristics of the avian influenza A (H7N9) virus on May 31, 2013, accessible as a PDF document as of September 29, 2014. 3. Heymann D. edited the Control of Communicable Disease Manual, 19th edition, published by the American Public Health Association in Washington in 2008. 4. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published a report titled Chikungunya fever: a re-emerging disease in Asia in New Delhi, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 5. Halstead SB, Scanlon JE, Umpaivit P, and Udomsakdi S conducted epidemiologic studies on dengue and chikungunya viruses in humans in Thailand from 1962 to 1964, focusing on the Bangkok Metropolitan area. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1969 (Volume 18, Issue 6, Pages 997-1021). 6. The WHO released a fact sheet on chikungunya (Fact Sheet No. 327) in 2014, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 7. The WHO published a fact sheet on Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (Fact Sheet No. 208) in 2013, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 8. Patel AK et al. documented the first outbreak of Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in India in the Journal of the Association of Physicians of India in September 2011 (Volume 59, Pages 585-589). 9. The WHO released a fact sheet on dengue and severe dengue (Fact Sheet No. 117) in 2014, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 10. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published a dengue fact sheet in New Delhi, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 11. The WHO provided information on dengue virus control on its website, accessible as of September 29, 2014. 12. Isaacson M, Sureau P, Courteille G, and Pattyn SR described the clinical aspects of Ebola virus disease at Ngalieema Hospital, Kinshasa, Zaire, in 1976. 13. The WHO released a fact sheet on Ebola virus disease (Fact Sheet No. 103) in 2014, accessible online as of July 29, 2014. 14. The WHO reported on Ebola Reston in pigs and humans in the Philippines in 2009, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 15. Olival KJ et al. identified Ebola virus antibodies in fruit bats in Bangladesh, with findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in February 2013 (Volume 19, Issue 2, Pages 270-273). 16. Nidom CA et al. provided serological evidence of Ebola virus infection in Indonesian orangutans, published in PLoS One in 2012 (Volume 7, Issue 7, Article e40740). 17. Zhang Y et al. isolated and characterized hantavirus carried by Apodemus peninsulae in Jilin, China, with findings published in the Journal of General Virology in 2007 (Volume 88, Pages 1295-1301). 18. The WHO provided information on hantavirus diseases in its International Travel and Health publication, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 19. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) detailed the story of Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) on its website, accessible as of September 29, 2014. 20. The WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific published a guide on the clinical management and public health response for hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in 2011, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 21. The WHO released a manual for the laboratory diagnosis of Japanese encephalitis virus infection in 2007, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 22. The WHO provided recommendations to ensure the quality, safety, and efficacy of Japanese encephalitis vaccines (live, attenuated) for human use, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 23. The WHO published a fact sheet on Japanese encephalitis as part of its water-related diseases series, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 24. The CDC provided an overview of Japanese encephalitis in its infectious diseases related to travel section, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 25. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published frequently asked questions on Japanese encephalitis in New Delhi, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 26. Gurley E et al. documented person-to-person transmission of Nipah virus in a Bangladeshi community, published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2007 (Volume 13, Pages 1031-1037). 27. Goh KJ et al. described the clinical features of Nipah virus encephalitis among pig farmers in Malaysia, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2000 (Volume 342, Pages 1229-1235). 28. The WHO provided standard precautions in healthcare as an aide-memoire, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 29. The WHO released frequently asked questions on Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 30. The WHO provided updates and risk assessments on MERS-CoV, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 31. The WHO published a fact sheet on rabies (Fact Sheet No. 99) in 2013, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 32. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia developed a strategic framework for the elimination of human rabies transmitted by dogs in the region, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 33. The WHO provided information on Rift Valley fever, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 34. Heymann DL discussed arthropod-borne viral fevers in the Control of Communicable Diseases Manual, 19th edition, published in 2008 (Pages 52-55). 35. The CDC published a fact sheet on Rift Valley fever, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 36. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia released a regional strategy for the prevention and control of viral hepatitis in 2013, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 37. Wong DC et al. provided evidence for non-A, non-B hepatitis etiology in India, published in The Lancet in 1980 (Volume 2, Pages 876-879). 38. The WHO released a fact sheet on hepatitis A (Fact Sheet No. 328) in 2014, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 39. Meng XJ discussed hepatitis E as a zoonosis in Viral Hepatitis, 3rd edition, edited by Thomas H, Zuckermann A, and Lemon S, published by Blackwell Publishing Ltd in 2006 (Pages 611-623). 40. The WHO provided a fact sheet on hepatitis E (Fact Sheet No. 280) in 2014, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 41. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia mapped neglected tropical diseases in the region in its Communicable Disease Newsletter (January 2011, Volume 8, Issue 1). 42. The WHO provided information on immunization, vaccines, and biological research and development, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 43. The CDC provided information for healthcare providers on anthrax, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 44. The United States Department of Agriculture published a fact sheet on foodborne illness and disease, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 45. The WHO reported on botulism in Thailand in 2006, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 46. The CDC provided emergency preparedness and response information on botulism, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 47. The WHO published a fact sheet on botulism in 2013, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 48. The Public Health Agency of Canada provided information on botulism, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 49. Pappas G et al. mapped the global distribution of human brucellosis, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2006 (Volume 6, Pages 91-99). 50. The WHO provided information on brucellosis as a health topic, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 51. Corbel MJ discussed brucellosis in humans and animals in a WHO publication from 2006, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 52. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published a fact sheet on leptospirosis in New Delhi, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 53. The CDC provided information on listeriosis, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 54. Ereno IL et al. reported a case of melioidosis, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 55. Heymann DL discussed melioidosis in the Control of Communicable Diseases Manual, last updated on September 24, 2010, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 56. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published operational guidelines on plague surveillance, diagnosis, prevention, and control in 2009, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 57. The WHO provided information on notification and reporting requirements under the International Health Regulations (2005), accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 58. The WHO published a fact sheet on non-typhoidal Salmonella (Fact Sheet No. 139), revised in April 2005, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 59. Aarestrup FM discussed antimicrobial resistance in food animals in Denmark, published in APMIS Supplement in 2000 (Volume 101, Pages 1-48). 60. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published frequently asked questions on scrub typhus, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 61. The WHO recommended surveillance standards in its second edition, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 62. Amornrut Leelaporn et al. reported the emergence of Francisella novicida bacteremia in Thailand, published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in December 2008 (Volume 14, Issue 12, Pages 1935-1937). 63. Nigrovic LE and Wingert SL discussed tularemia in Infectious Disease Clinics of North America in September 2008 (Volume 22, Issue 3, Pages 489-504). 64. Keim P et al. explored the molecular epidemiology, evolution, and ecology of Francisella, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences in June 2007 (Volume 1105, Pages 30-66). 65. The WHO published a fact sheet on taeniasis/cysticercosis (Fact Sheet No. 376) in 2014, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 66. The CDC provided information on toxoplasmosis, accessible online as of September 29, 2014. 67. Kaewpitoon N et al. discussed the distribution of trichinosis in Thailand, published in the World Journal of Gastroenterology in June 2008 (Volume 14, Issue 22, Pages 3471-3475). 68. Sethi B et al. reported on human trichinosis in Uttarakhand, India, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Sciences in March 2010 (Volume 64, Issue 3, Pages 104-110).
